samples.summary: `expandCellRangeForMerges` stays unbounded (`budgetCells = Infinity`) on every non-paint caller, over a table whose size and merge shape a peer chooses — a hostile table can hang the tab on copy/cut/delete/merge and on every mousemove of a drag
samples.evidence: The new `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` budget is opt-in and only `computeSelectionRects` passes it (selection.ts:715). Every other caller keeps the `Infinity` default: `text-editor.ts:3324`, `:3967`, `:3991` (drag / Shift+Arrow handlers, invoked per pointer/key event), `table-merge-context.ts:53` (reached from `getTableMergeContext`, editor.ts:4392, which the toolbar re-reads on selection change), and `normalizeCellRange` on the copy/cut/delete path via `Selection.getNormalizedRange`. The scan is a fixed-point `while (changed)` loop over the rectangle (selection.ts:135-141) where each `colSpan === 0` orphan cell calls `findMergeTopLeftBudgeted` (selection.ts:155), which rescans everything above-left of it. Row count is structure, not an attribute, so no numeric band reaches it — a collaborator (the same actor the rest of this change defends against) can write a table with tens of thousands of rows whose cells all carry `colSpan: 0` with no owner; a user who then selects a large rectangle in it and presses Delete or Ctrl+C drives O(area²) work with no ceiling and no way to abort. The file's own comment acknowledges the tradeoff ("a slow gesture" is preferred to a short rectangle) but the chosen alternative is an unbounded loop on peer-shaped data, i.e. the exact hazard class the nesting cap closes elsewhere. A bounded-but-correct answer (e.g. budget = table area + 1, or refusing the command past the budget) would keep correctness without leaving the loop open.

samples.summary: `insertTableRow` / `insertTableColumn` write rows and cells under a table at or past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with no refusal, manufacturing the 'rows no reader reads' state that then makes `updateBlock` / `updateTableCell` / `writeFullDocument` throw for every collaborator
samples.evidence: `buildBlockNode` refuses to emit rows past the cap and `writeFullDocument`/`updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` refuse to *replace* a range holding truncated rows, but `insertTableRow` (line 2933-2942) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2981) compute `rowDepth` only to pass it down — neither compares it to `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` — and then `editByPath` a row/cell node straight into a table block whose own depth may be >= the cap. The branch's own test does exactly this to build its fixture (`packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts`, `peerRowsPastTheCap`: `insertBlockAfter` a table at the cap, then `insertTableRow` into it), so the state is reachable through the store's public API, not only through raw Yorkie ops. Once it exists, every honest client that reads the document back gets `rows: []` for that table, and any write that replaces the enclosing range — `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `setHeader`/`setFooter`, and `writeFullDocument` (hence `setDocument`, i.e. applying an import) — throws `truncatedRowsError()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1752, 3462). The result is a document region, and for full writes a whole document, that is permanently unwritable for all collaborators; the backend twin is `writeDocsRoot` throwing and `DocumentCopyService` refusing the copy. Blocking the creating writer (refuse to insert a row/cell under a table at the cap, as the other producers do) is what would keep the refusal from being reachable in the first place.

samples.summary: `writeDocsRoot` enforces the nesting invariant with a bare `Error`, so any backend caller that does not pre-check gets a 500 instead of a 4xx; the invariant is enforced caller-by-caller rather than at the sink
samples.evidence: The refusal at docs-tree.ts:376-382 throws `new Error(...)`, not an `HttpException`. It is currently unreachable from `PUT /content` only because `assertValidBlock` rejects the body first (docs-content.controller.ts:454) and from the copy route only because `DocumentCopyService` added its own `BadRequestException` before calling it (document-copy.service.ts:446). Every future caller of this exported writer — the seed path at `template/seed/seed-templates.ts:79` already calls it unguarded — turns a content-shape problem into an unhandled 500 (and, in NestJS, a stack-trace-bearing error log) rather than a client error. Throwing a `BadRequestException` here, or having the callers share one guard, would make the sink itself the enforcement point.

samples.summary: The revision-snapshot normalizer's depth counter only increments on `row` nodes, so a snapshot nesting any other node type (`cell`, `block`, `inline`) deeply still recurses unbounded; the safety argument is delegated to an SDK parser limit the comment itself calls one release away from changing
samples.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (snapshot-adapters.ts:158-166) bounds recursion only via `isRow && depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`; a node chain of `cell > cell > cell …` or `block > block > …` — perfectly representable in a snapshot, which is data any collaborator's writes produced and which is parsed in the viewer's tab — increments nothing and recurses to the chain's full depth. The mitigation stated in the docstring is that `YSON.parse` gives out first, which is an empirical property of `@yorkie-js/sdk` rather than an invariant of this code. Worst case is a `RangeError` in the revision preview (which `RevisionPreview` renders as an alert), so impact is contained, but the cap as written does not bound the walk it claims to bound.

samples.summary: The paint budget is per peer per paint, so the bound scales with the number of connected peers
samples.evidence: `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS = 1 << 18` (262,144 cell visits) is charged once per peer selection per frame (`computeSelectionRects` is called in a loop over `peerCursors`, editor.ts:2094-2105). With a few dozen collaborators all holding cell rectangles in a pathological table, the per-frame ceiling is millions of cell visits — bounded, but well past a frame budget. A shared per-frame budget, or a much smaller per-peer one, would bound the amplification rather than one peer's share of it.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `expandCellRangeForMerges` defaults `budgetCells = Infinity` (selection.ts:126) and only `computeSelectionRects` passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` (selection.ts:715). All other entry points run unbounded: `normalizeCellRange`/`normalizeRange` default to Infinity (selection.ts:205, 265) on the copy/cut/delete path via `Selection.getNormalizedRange`, plus `text-editor.ts:3324` (Shift+Arrow, per keypress), `text-editor.ts:3967`/`:3991` (pointer drag resolution, per move), and `table-merge-context.ts:53` (read path re-run on selection change). The loop at selection.ts:135-161 is a fixed-point rescan whose `colSpan === 0` branch calls `findMergeTopLeftBudgeted` (selection.ts:155), which at selection.ts:90-103 scans every cell above-left; with `Infinity` the `--budget.left <= 0` check at selection.ts:92 never fires, so work is superlinear in table area. The shape is attacker-controlled: `crdt-tree.ts:196` preserves peer-written `colSpan: 0` orphans verbatim, and no read boundary bands the row count (only MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS=256 / MAX_TABLE_SPAN=1000 at numeric-attrs.ts:92-95 and nesting depth), so a collaborator can write a table with tens of thousands of orphan-covered rows. A local user who then selects a large rectangle and presses Delete/Ctrl+C, or simply drags, drives O(area^2) work with no ceiling and no abort — an untrusted-input-driven availability hang, the same hazard class the file's own budget, the numeric bands, and the nesting cap exist to close. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present, nothing guards the unbounded callers (the in-file comment at selection.ts:20-52 documents the tradeoff but is not a guard, and layout is only linear in table area while this scan is superlinear), and untrusted-input DoS is within the security lens.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described — `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) obtain `rowDepth` from `resolveTableRowDepth` (2875-2884) and pass it to `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` without comparing it to `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, while `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` (1748-1752) and `writeFullDocument` (3429-3436) throw `truncatedRowsError()` (503-509) on such a range. But this is not a Security-lens defect. (1) The impact is availability/state-consistency — a region or document that later refuses writes — with no authorization gate, secret, injection sink, crypto/signature check, SSRF or deserialization anywhere on the path; `insertTableRow` only computes numeric tree indices and calls `editByPath` (2941, 2975-2979). That is the rubric's explicit "general logic bugs (correctness lens)" exclusion, and it matches none of the critical/major security anchors. (2) The nesting caps in this file are client-side advisory guards in a browser-resident CRDT store, not an enforced boundary: any actor with write access can emit Yorkie tree ops directly and produce the identical state regardless of a check in `insertTableRow`, so its absence is not an auth/validation bypass. The enforceable twins already exist server-side (backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:179,237,379; backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:454). (3) Non-adversarial reachability is already bounded by model/editor/import refusals (docs/src/model/document.ts:925, docs/src/view/editor.ts:4232, docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:437). The defect is real and is already carried as a confirmed finding in the correctness lane (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:6); I am removing it only from the security gate.
